question.problem: The variances of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are $0.09$ and $0.16$, respectively. Given that $\text{Cov}(X,Y)=-0.03,$ find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{0.09}=0.3, \\ \text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[Y]}=\sqrt{0.16}=0.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting our data in the formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[X]} \\  & =\frac{-0.03}{0.3\cdot 0.4} \\  & =-0.25.\end{aligned}
$$
